'''''Polaskia''''' (named after [[United States|America]]n amateur [[Charles Polaski]]) is a [[genus]] of tree-like [[cactus|cacti]] reaching 4–5 m high, comprising 2 [[species]]. Both present primitive characteristics, but ''[[Polaskia chichipe]]'' is nearer to ''[[Myrtillocactus]]'' while ''[[Polaskia chende]]'' is nearer to ''[[Stenocereus]]''. The genus is found in the [[Mexico|Mexican]] states of [[Puebla]] and [[Oaxaca]].<ref name="Anderson Eggli 2005 p. ">{{cite book | last=Anderson | first=Edward F. | last2=Eggli | first2=Urs | title=Das große Kakteen-Lexikon | publication-place=Stuttgart | date=2005 | isbn=978-3-8001-4573-7 | oclc=181456857 | language=de | page=}}</ref><ref name="On-line Guide to the positive identification of Members of the Cactus Family">{{cite web | title=On-line Guide to the positive identification of Members of the Cactus Family | website=On-line Guide to the positive identification of Members of the Cactus Family | url=https://cactiguide.com/cactus/?genus=Polaskia | access-date=2022-10-25}}</ref>
==Description==
The tree-like, highly branched species of the Polaskia genus reach heights of growth of between 4 and 5 meters and form dense crowns 3 to 4 meters above the ground. Its bright green shoots repeatedly fork and grow 1 to 2 meters long. The 7 to 12 ribs are sharply triangular in cross-section. On their edges, these wear 3 to 4 millimeters wide, shield-shaped areoles at close intervals. The central spine may be absent. The 3 to 8 radial spines are greyish to blackish.

The urn- to bell-shaped flowers are white to creamy white to yellowish green. They open day and night and are between 4 and 6 centimeters long.

The red, spherical fruits with a diameter of 2 to 4 centimeters are juicy and edible. The small seeds it contains are pear- to ovoid-shaped and dull black.
==Synonymy==
The following genera have been brought into [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonymy]] with ''Polaskia'': 
*''Chichipia'' <small>[[Backeb.]]</small> (nom. inval.)
